paragraphs.label: a
paragraphs.anchor: who can withhold himself from speaking

paragraphs.text: You have comforted others in their afflictions but you cannot now comfort yourself.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: He concludes that Job was a hypocrite and had no true fear or trust in God.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: He concludes that Job was reproved seeing that God handles him so extremely, which is the argument that the carnal men make against the children of God.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: They who do evil cannot but receive evil.
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: He shows that God needs no great preparation to destroy his enemies: for he can do it with the blast of his mouth.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: Though men according to their office do not punish tyrants (whom for their cruelty he compares to lions, and their children to their whelps) yet God is able and his justice will punish them.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: A thing I did not know before was declared to me by vision, that is that whoever thinks himself just will be found a sinner when he comes before God.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: In these visions which God shows to his creatures, there is always a certain fear joined, that the authority of it might be had in greater reverence.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: When all things were quiet or when the fear was relieved as God appeared to Elijah, 1Ki 19:12.
paragraphs.label: k

paragraphs.text: He proves that if God punished the innocent, the creature would be more just than the creator, which was blasphemy.
paragraphs.label: l

paragraphs.text: If God finds imperfection in his angels when they are not maintained by his power, how much more shall he lay folly to man's charge when he would justify himself against God?
paragraphs.label: m

paragraphs.text: That is, in this mortal body, subject to corruption, as in 2Co 5:1.
paragraphs.label: n

paragraphs.text: They see death continually before their eyes and daily approaching them.
paragraphs.label: o

paragraphs.text: No man for all this considers it.
paragraphs.label: p

paragraphs.text: That is, before any of them were so wise, as to think of death.
paragraphs.label: q
